text: Impression [Lat. impressus ]: Ger. Eindruck ; Fr. impression ; Ital. impressione . (1) Used by Hume to designate experiences of the perceptual order as contrasted with 'ideas' (fainter revived impressions). (2) The physiological process of stimulation apart from the corresponding sensation which it arouses. (3) In sociology: sometimes used for CONSTRAINT (q.v.). ( J.M.B. , G.F.S. )
